Issues.Title: fix(core): respect @Host boundary in embedded view injector lookup
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: Fixes #57390

When an embedded view is created with a custom injector (`createEmbeddedView(..., { injector })` or `*ngTemplateOutlet="...; injector: ..."`), the `HasEmbeddedViewInjector` flag is set on the view and inherited by descendant component views.
When resolving tokens, `lookupTokenUsingEmbeddedInjector` walks up the view tree without checking `InternalInjectFlags.Host`. This allows resolutions with `@Host()` on directives inside child components within the embedded view to bypass the host component boundary and leak into the custom embedded view injector and its parent injector hierarchy (such as finding an ancestor reactive `FormGroupDirective` providing `ControlContainer`, causing NG01050/NG01350).

## What is the new behavior?

In `lookupTokenUsingEmbeddedInjector`, stop searching parent nodes once the host element node (`hostTElementNode = flags & InternalInjectFlags.Host ? lView[DECLARATION_COMPONENT_VIEW][T_HOST] : null`) has been checked when `InternalInjectFlags.Host` is set.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): place standalone self-reference at index 0 and preserve forwardRef closure
Issues.Body:
### Before

Standalone component self-references in `ngp` diverged from `ngtsc` in three ways:
1. If a recursive standalone component listed itself in `@Component.imports` after another dependency (e.g. `imports: [DirA, TreeComponent]`), `TreeComponent` remained at its `imports` position instead of index `0`:
   ```ts
   dependencies: [DirA, TreeComponent],
   ```
2. If a standalone component imported itself via `forwardRef(() => ForwardTreeComponent)`, `isExpressionForwardReference` unconditionally returned `false` for `d.name === className`, omitting the closure wrapper:
   ```ts
   dependencies: [DirA, ForwardTreeComponent],
   ```
3. Self-deduplication checked only `d.name === className` and `d.ref.consumerImport == null`, which collided with an aliased cross-file import whose exported class name matched `className` (`import { SameNameComp as OtherSameNameComp }`).

### After

1. Standalone components filter any explicit self-import (`d.name === className && d.ref.localAlias === className && d.ref.consumerImport == null`) and `unshift` the component's own declaration to index `0` in both `processor.ts` and `tcb_adapter.ts`, matching `StandaloneComponentScopeReader` in `ngtsc`:
   ```ts
   dependencies: [TreeComponent, DirA],
   ```
2. `standaloneImportMayBeForwardDeclared` is computed from `resolvedDeclarations` before self-deduplication and included in `hasForwardRef`, preserving the closure wrapper when `forwardRef` is used in `@Component.imports`:
   ```ts
   dependencies: (): any => [ForwardTreeComponent, DirA],
   ```
3. Aliased cross-file imports sharing the same exported class name are preserved alongside the component's self-reference:
   ```ts
   dependencies: [SameNameComp, OtherSameNameComp],
   ```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler-cli): place standalone self-reference at index 0 and preserve forwardRef closure" (#71404)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): avoid spurious forwardRef closure for re-exported NgModule deps
Issues.Body:
### Before

In `ng-analyze`'s `contextualize_ngmodule_scope_declarations`, when a non-standalone `@Component` precedes its declaring `@NgModule` in the same file, every relative cross-file declaration transitively exported by an imported `@NgModule` was marked `is_forward_ref = true`, causing `ngp` to wrap `dependencies` in a closure (`dependencies: () => [i1.FeatureComponent]`) even when all template dependencies are imported at the top of the file:

```ts
dependencies: (): any => [i1.FeatureComponent],
```

### After

Cross-file declarations in an `@NgModule` scope are only marked `is_forward_ref = true` when they have a local identifier in the component's file (`contextual_decl.ref_meta.local_alias.is_some()`) and the declaring `@NgModule` is in the same file after the component, matching `ngtsc`'s `LocalIdentifierStrategy` and `isExpressionForwardReference`:

```ts
dependencies: [i1.FeatureComponent],
```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler-cli): avoid spurious forwardRef closure for re-exported NgModule deps" (#71403)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): check `@defer` blocks in the control flow content projection diagnostic
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements: - [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) ## PR Type What kind of change does this PR introduce? - [x] Bugfix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables) - [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes) - [ ] Build related changes - [ ] CI related changes - [ ] Documentation content changes - [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes - [ ] Other... Please describe: ## What is the current behavior? The content of a `@defer` block always goes to the default `ng-content` slot, because the block doesn't copy the tag name and attributes of its root node (#58110, tracked in #64504). NG8011 doesn't check `@defer` blocks, so this happens without any warning: ```html @defer {

Title

} ``` `

` is projected into the default slot instead of `[card-title]`, or not rendered if the component has no default slot. Issue Number: Fixes #71397 ## What is the new behavior? `TcbControlFlowContentProjectionOp` also goes through the `@defer` blocks of the element, including their `@placeholder`, `@loading` and `@error` blocks, and reports each root node that matches a specific slot. Unlike the other blocks, a single root node is reported too, since it isn't projected either. The suggestions in the existing message (keep a single root node) don't apply here, so the out-of-band recorder gets a separate `deferredBlockPreventingContentProjection` method. It uses the same error code and the same `controlFlowPreventingContentProjection` option, and points to `ngProjectAs`: ``` Node matches the "[card-title]" slot of the "Card" component, but will not be projected into the specific slot because it is inside a @defer block. The content of @defer blocks, including their @placeholder, @loading and @error blocks, is always projected into the default slot, or not rendered if the component doesn't have one. To project the node in the right slot, wrap the @defer block in an with an "ngProjectAs" attribute that matches the "[card-title]" selector. ``` I added four tests: the main block, the secondary blocks, content that only matches the catch-all slot, and the `ngProjectAs` workaround. The two that expect a diagnostic fail without the change. Like the other specs of this diagnostic, they're listed in `ngp_known_failures.ts`. ## Does this PR introduce a breaking change? - [ ] Yes - [x] No ## Other information The generated code doesn't change. The new warning only shows up for a `@defer` block placed directly inside a component with `ng-content` selectors, when one of its root nodes matches a specific selector. That node is already in the wrong slot today, so each warning points to a real bug, but it can be new on code that compiles cleanly now. If that's a problem for the internal rollout, I can retarget the PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(compiler): check `@defer` blocks in the control flow content projection diagnostic" (#71398)

Issues.Title: Ability to configure custom JSON parser in HttpClient - Back again!
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

common

### Description

As stated in [the issue 48167](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/48167), there are use cases where being able to inject a custom JSON parser for HttpClient would be beneficial, and a simple solution was already provided in [this PR](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/25027).
If I take the time to write this issue, it's because I came across yet another use case: supporting circular references. I'm currently developing an app that communicates with a .NET API, which maps objects to JSON with references (using $id and $ref). So currently, with HttpClient's native JSON parser, I get objects which contain $id and $ref properties, and I have 2 options : either reconstruct the reference tree from the objects after parsing, or implement my own interceptor to set the references while parsing. And so, as stated, in the previous issue, I have to copy-paste a bunch of code to make sure to implement everything correctly (XSSI_PREFIX, null for empty response body, error handling).
And finally, [a similar issue](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/21079) was opened 9 years ago. It received, as well as the other one opened in 2022, a great number of upvotes. The reason stated each time for not implementing this feature is that it's "fairly straightforward to do via an interceptor". I think the key word here is "fairly". It's not that simple, and it's useless error-prone copy-pasting done by every developer.
Given all of that, I come to the following conclusion: the need exists, and a simple solution is already implemented. So, why not do it?

### Proposed solution

Accepting [the pull request 25027](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/25027).

### Alternatives considered

- Add the interceptor provided in [issue 48167](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/48167) to the library, so that it can be easily subclassed by a developer to safely implement they own parsing.
- Implement a feature for my specific use case: handling of the "$id-$ref" reference system directly in the native JSON parser.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Ability to configure custom JSON parser in HttpClient - Back again!" (#71399)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): report unsupported `animate.` bindings
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The compiler accepts any name after `animate.` and compiles everything other than `animate.enter` as a leave animation. A misspelled `animate.entr="fade-in"` compiles to `ɵɵanimateLeave("fade-in")` without any error: the element doesn't animate when it's added, and plays `fade-in` while it's being removed.

Issue Number: Fixes #71393

## What is the new behavior?

Any `animate.` name other than `animate.enter` and `animate.leave` is reported:

```
Unsupported animation binding "animate.entr". The supported animation bindings are "animate.enter" and "animate.leave".
```

The message comes from `getUnsupportedAnimationBindingError`, which is used everywhere such a name can come in:

- `BindingParser.validateAnimationName` for property and event bindings, in templates and in the `host` object.
- The template transform for static and interpolated attributes (`animate.entr="..."`), which don't go through those paths.
- `verifyHostBindings` for static attributes in the `host` object.
- ngtsc's `extractHostBindings` for `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener`. JIT already verifies the names from the decorators together with the `host` object, AOT didn't, so without this the two would disagree.

A two-way binding to an `animate.` name now gets its own error, reported once, instead of being compiled as a property binding plus a leave listener for the generated `<name>Change` event:

```
Unsupported two-way binding on "animate.enter". Animations can only be bound with a static value, a property binding or an event binding.
```

Tests: two in `r3_template_transform_spec` (every template form, and two-way bindings, each checked to be reported exactly once), and three in `ngtsc_spec` (templates, the `host` object, `@HostBinding`/`@HostListener`). They fail without the change.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Code that compiled before can now fail: a template, `host` object or decorator that uses another `animate.` name or a two-way binding on one. That includes libraries published in partial compilation mode, since the linker parses their templates again, and JIT/TestBed. Those bindings never did what they said, so I'd expect every hit to be a bug, which is why I left "No" above, but I can mark it as breaking or land it differently if you prefer.

Two related cases are left as they are, because they also affect the valid names and change the meaning of existing code: `[attr.animate.*]` bindings and `animate.*` attributes inside `ngNonBindable` are still compiled as animations.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler): report unsupported `animate.` bindings" (#71394)

Issues.Title: Enrich prod-errors in Signals with specific problem
Issues.Body: ### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request? core ### Description Hey team. Currently, errors occurring within `computed/linkedSignal` lack any information about the nature of the error itself in the prod: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/92e5aa8f154096a756757d0e295cde4299788650/packages/core/primitives/signals/src/computed.ts#L136 As a result, the error signature in Sentry is uninformative, making it impossible to determine where an error originated without examining the stack traces: Furthermore, when errors arise from different locations (for instance, from `computed` and `linkedSignal`) it becomes difficult to distinguish between them in Sentry’s error lists (though Sentry’s built-in grouping mechanism does [at least separate them](https://docs.sentry.io/concepts/data-management/event-grouping/#grouping-by-stack-trace)), which complicates the process of locating and debugging errors. ### Proposed solution For each error, add a code instead of a message, as has already been done for `RuntimeError` ### Alternatives considered I know why [it has been done](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/44210#pullrequestreview-810615849), but maybe it is possible to simplify (shorten) error messages in all modes and remove the `ngDevMode` at all.

Issues.Title: fix(core): check every i18n attribute translation for ICUs
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows Angular's guidelines.
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (see below).
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (not applicable: no API change).

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

`i18nAttributesFirstPass` rejects attribute translations that contain an ICU:

```ts
const ICU_REGEXP = /({\s*�\d+:?\d*�\s*,\s*\S{6}\s*,[\s\S]*})/gi;
...
if (ICU_REGEXP.test(message)) {
  throw new Error(`ICU expressions are not supported in attributes. Message: "${message}".`);
}
```

Because of the `g` flag, a successful `test()` leaves `lastIndex` at the end of the match. That success is always followed by the throw, so nothing resets it. The next attribute message is then searched from that offset. If it is shorter, the ICU is skipped, `test()` returns `false`, and the translation renders instead of throwing.

`ICU_REGEXP` has no other use in the file, so nothing depends on the `g` flag.

## What is the new behavior?

The `g` flag is dropped, so every check starts at index 0 and every attribute ICU is rejected.

## Tests

Added a case under `invalid translations handling` in `acceptance/i18n_spec.ts`. It renders a long title whose translation has an ICU, then a short one.

I couldn't run Bazel locally, so I reproduced the same scenario against the published `@angular/core@21.2.25` bundle with the real `loadTranslations` + TestBed:

| | long title | short title |
|---|---|---|
| as published (`/gi`) | throws | **renders** |
| with `/i` | throws | throws |

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(core): check every i18n attribute translation for ICUs" (#71389)

## What is the current behavior?

Follow-up to #70266. `TransferState` now keeps keys such as `__proto__` in a null-prototype dictionary and round-trips them through `toJson`, but `getTransferState` in `packages/core/src/render3/util/transfer_state_utils.ts` (published as `ng.ɵgetTransferState` for DevTools) still copies the restored entries into a plain object literal. For a serialized state like `{"__proto__":{"cached":true},"constructor":"state"}` the copy assigns through the inherited `__proto__` setter: the entry is missing from the returned object, the stored value becomes its prototype so `cached` shows up as an inherited property, and under Node's `--disable-proto=throw` the copy throws. The DevTools backend then merges each root's result into another plain object with `Object.assign`, which drops the entry a second time.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

`getTransferState` builds its result with the existing `createDictionary` helper, and the DevTools merge target is a null-prototype object, so prototype-named keys stay ordinary entries all the way to the Transfer State tab.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

The new spec in `transfer_state_spec.ts` fails on `main` (`Object.keys` is `['constructor']` and the prototype is the stored object) and passes with the change; `//packages/core/test:test` and the Chromium run of `//devtools/projects/ng-devtools-backend/src/lib:client_event_subscribers_test` are green locally.

Issues.Title: docs: fix wrong claims and examples in the forms guides
Issues.Body:
Several statements and snippets in the forms guides don't match the framework.

- `FormBuilder` has four factory methods, not three: `control()`, `group()`, `record()` and `array()`.
- The `FormArrayDirective` example uses `[formArray]` and `formControlName` but never imports `ReactiveFormsModule`, so it doesn't work as written.
- In the signal forms validation guide, `a@b` is a valid email. Only `a@` triggers both `email()` and `minLength(5)`.
- The dynamic forms tutorial says `QuestionControlService` collects several `FormGroup` instances and that the question component creates form groups. The service builds one `FormGroup` of `FormControl`s, and the component only receives it. The tutorial also calls the button "Submit", but the example renders "Save".
- The forms overview tests step through change detection, but the example specs only call `await fixture.whenStable()`.
- The NG01354 page shows `viewProviders` with `FormGroupDirective` as a way to register `ngModel`. `NgModel` throws when its parent is a reactive form directive (`modelParentException`), so I replaced that example with `formControlName` or the standalone option.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs: fix wrong claims and examples in the forms guides" (#71383)

Issues.Title: docs: fix the compile errors in the migration examples
Issues.Body:
Several before and after examples on the migration pages don't compile when you copy them.

- Signal queries: `ElementRef` is used but not imported, and the template reads `someRef` (the query selector) instead of the member `ref`.
- Standalone: the "After" `main.ts` imports `App` from `./app`, but the component file is `./app/app`.
- RouterTestingModule: `TestBed` is used in all four examples but never imported.
- Inject: `@Component()` has no argument, but the decorator requires one. It's now `@Component({template: ''})`.

Issues.Title: fix(router): escape colons in parenthesized primary child segments
Issues.Body: When a non-root route group has both a primary child and a sibling named outlet, `DefaultUrlSerializer` serializes the primary child inside parentheses without an outlet prefix, causing a colon in its first segment (e.g. `/x/(admin:y//aux:z)`) to be misparsed on round-trip as a named outlet delimiter. We resolve this by escaping colons in the first segment of an unprefixed primary child as `%3A`.

Issues.Title: feat(router): add navigate method to RouterTestingHarness
Issues.Body:
Mirrors `Router.navigate` so tests can pass `queryParams`, `fragment` and other `NavigationExtras` without an extra navigation.

## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [ ] Bugfix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [x] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [x] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

`RouterTestingHarness` only exposes `navigateByUrl`, which accepts a string. To set query params or a fragment, tests must build the URL string by hand or inject `Router` and perform an extra navigation

Issue Number: #71210 

## What is the new behavior?

Adds `RouterTestingHarness.navigate(commands, extras?, requiredRoutedComponentType?)`, mirroring `Router.navigate`. It accepts `NavigationExtras` (e.g. `queryParams`, `fragment`), waits for the navigation and any redirects to complete, and returns the activated component. Passing a component type enforces it, as with `navigateByUrl`

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->

## Other information

The new private helper `runNavigation` consolidates the logic shared by `navigateByUrl` and `navigate`: waiting for the navigation and redirects, running change detection, and resolving or type-checking the activated component. The two public methods only supply the router call

Existing `navigateByUrl` usages in the repo's tests are intentionally left unchanged

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): use distinct chunk naming for web worker bundles
Issues.Body:
Previously, `bundleWebWorker` inherited `chunkNames` from the main esbuild configuration while bundling web workers in a separate synchronous esbuild pass. When both the main application bundle and a web worker dynamically imported modules that shared a common dependency, esbuild generated a shared chunk with identical content and the same `chunk-[hash].js` filename in both builds. During post-build chunk optimization, Rolldown traced only the main application entrypoint, merged the shared chunk into new optimized chunks, and removed the original `chunk-[hash].js` file from the build outputs while the unoptimized web worker chunks still imported it.

Setting `chunkNames` to `'worker-chunk-[hash]'` in `bundleWebWorker` ensures that chunks emitted for web workers have distinct filenames and do not collide with main bundle chunks during metafile merging or chunk optimization.

Closes #34292
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/build): use distinct chunk naming for web worker bundles" (#34379)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): use only the first value of the `X-Forwarded-Prefi…
Issues.Body:
The `X-Forwarded-Prefix` header is validated using its first comma-separated value, like the other `X-Forwarded-*` headers. However, redirects used the entire header value. With a trusted header, any value after the first one was added to the `Location` header without being validated.

The first value is now used wherever the header is read, which matches how `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Proto` and `X-Forwarded-Port` are handled.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): watch only explicitly added paths in chokidar watcher
Issues.Body:
When preserveSymlinks or polling is enabled, the build watcher falls back to Chokidar. Previously, createChokidarWatcher initialized Chokidar on the entire workspace root directory and expanded any watched file inside node_modules to its full package root directory via ChokidarNodeModulesManager. Because Chokidar v5 recursively walks watched directories and attaches individual fs.watch handles to every subdirectory and file, projects with many workspace subdirectories or large imported packages could exceed the macOS per-process directory watch limit and crash with an unhandled EMFILE error.

This change initializes Chokidar with an empty watch set and registers only the specific paths passed to add() and remove(), eliminating recursive directory scans across the workspace root and node_modules packages. When a directory is explicitly watched (such as when NG_BUILD_WATCH_ROOT is enabled), node_modules subdirectories are pruned unless directly added to the watch set. An error listener is also attached to prevent unhandled watcher errors from terminating the process, and removed files that remain in the watch set are re-registered so subsequent file recreation is detected across multiple watched directories.

Closes #34312
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/build): watch only explicitly added paths in chokidar watcher" (#34361)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): match proxy glob patterns against URL pathname only
Issues.Body:
When normalizing proxy configurations for Vite, glob patterns are converted into regular expression strings using picomatch. Because picomatch builds regular expressions assuming the input is a file path and anchors them with `$`, whereas Vite tests regex proxy keys against `req.url` (which includes any query string), requests with query parameters could fail to match glob entries such as `/search/**` or `/api/*.json`, or inadvertently match wildcards against query string parameters.

Adapt the generated regular expression so that wildcard tokens do not match across the `?` query delimiter and end-of-path anchors allow an optional query string after the matched pathname.

Closes #34257
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/build): match proxy glob patterns against URL pathname only" (#34377)

The third-party `server` builder warning also printed the `build` target's builder instead of the `server` target's builder.

Issues.Title: Angular SSR redirects can take healthy proxies upstreams out of rotation through an unbounded Location header
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Angular SSR redirects can take healthy proxies upstreams out of rotation through an unbounded Location header" (#34365)

Issues.Title: Fix SSR redirect location length
Issues.Body:
### fix(@angular/ssr): use only the first value of the X-Forwarded-Prefix header
The `X-Forwarded-Prefix` header is validated using its first
comma-separated value, like the other `X-Forwarded-*` headers. However,
redirects used the entire header value. With a trusted header, any
value after the first one was added to the `Location` header without
being validated.

The first value is now used wherever the header is read, which matches
how `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Proto` and `X-Forwarded-Port` are
handled.


### fix(@angular/ssr): limit the length of redirect locations

Redirects created on the server can contain data from the request.
Route redirects keep the path and the query string, redirects done by
the router while rendering use its final URL, and the
`X-Forwarded-Prefix` header is prepended. The router also encodes some
characters again, so the `Location` header can be several times longer
than the request URL.

Reverse proxies read the response headers into a buffer of limited
size, 4 KB by default in NGINX. When the headers do not fit, the proxy
returns a 502 and, with passive health checks, counts it against the
server. A few requests could take every server out of rotation.

`AngularAppEngine` and `AngularNodeAppEngine` now return a 400 when a
redirect location is longer than 2048 characters. The limit can be
changed with the new `maxRedirectLocationLength` option. Redirects
created while prerendering are not limited.

Fixes https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/issues/34365
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix SSR redirect location length" (#34366)

Issues.Title: @angular/build: lazy routes get no SSR modulepreload hints when the app's tsconfig is not at the workspace root (ɵentryName relative to basePath, chunk map relative to workspace root)
Issues.Body:
### Command build ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description When an application's `tsconfig.app.json` is not at the workspace root, SSR adds no `` for any lazy route. That includes the CLI's own multi-project layout (`ng generate application` puts it in `projects//`) and every Nx workspace. The routes are written in the shape `lazyRoutesTransformer` recognises, and the pages render correctly. Only the hints are missing, and nothing warns about it. **Cause.** The two sides of the lookup use different base directories: - `lazyRoutesTransformer` stamps `ɵentryName` as a path relative to `compilerOptions.basePath` ([`lazy-routes-transformer.ts#L151`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.3/packages/angular/build/src/tools/angular/transformers/lazy-routes-transformer.ts#L151)). The compiler sets `basePath` to the directory of the tsconfig, here `projects/site`. - `generateLazyLoadedFilesMappings` keys `entryPointToBrowserMapping` by esbuild's `entryPoint` ([`manifest.ts#L262`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.3/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/manifest.ts#L262)). That path is relative to `absWorkingDir`, which is the workspace root ([`application-code-bundle.ts#L631`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.3/packages/angular/build/src/tools/esbuild/application-code-bundle.ts#L631)). So the stamp reads `src/app/home/home.ts` and the key reads `projects/site/src/app/home/home.ts`. `appendPreloadToMetadata` finds nothing and every route's `preload` stays empty. When the tsconfig is at the workspace root, as in a default `ng new`, the two bases happen to coincide, which is probably why this has gone unnoticed. | `projects/site/tsconfig.app.json` | `ɵentryName` in the server bundle | `preload` in `angular-app-manifest.mjs` | route hints in `index.html` / `pricing/index.html` | | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | | as generated | `src/app/home/home.ts` | none | 0 / 0 | | `"angularCompilerOptions": { "basePath": "." }` added | `projects/site/src/app/home/home.ts` | on both routes | 1 / 1 (the route's own chunk) | **Workaround.** `"angularCompilerOptions": { "basePath": "." }` in the app's tsconfig. It works only because the value is read raw and resolved against the process cwd, and the build happens to run from the workspace root. **Expected.** Route hints do not depend on where the tsconfig lives. One option is for the transformer to stamp paths relative to the workspace root, which the builder already knows, instead of relative to `basePath`. **Real-world impact.** In our Nx workspace (22 lazy routes, `@nx/angular:application`, which delegates to `buildApplication` unchanged), no route had ever received a hint. With the workaround every route does. On the home page, the shell route's chunk finishes 5.8 s earlier in throttled Lighthouse runs (mobile, devtools throttling, 8× CPU, 5 runs), and TTI drops by 1.3 s. ### Minimal Reproduction ```bash npx -p @angular/cli@22.2.3 ng new ws --create-application=false --skip-git --package-manager=npm --defaults --ai-config=none cd ws npx ng generate application site --ssr --routing --style=css --skip-tests --defaults ``` `projects/site/src/app/app.routes.ts` ```ts import { Routes } from '@angular/router'; export const routes: Routes = [ { path: '', loadComponent: () => import('./home/home').then((m) => m.Home) }, { path: 'pricing', loadComponent: () => import('./pricing/pricing').then((m) => m.Pricing), }, ]; ``` `projects/site/src/app/home/home.ts` (and `pricing/pricing.ts`, the same with `Pricing`) ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; @Component({ selector: 'app-home', template: '

Home

' }) export class Home {} ``` ```bash npx ng build site grep -c '"preload"' dist/site/server/angular-app-manifest.mjs # 0 grep -o ']*>' dist/site/browser/index.html # only the shared initial chunk grep -rhoE 'entryName:"[^"]*"' dist/site/server/*.mjs # src/app/home/home.ts, src/app/pricing/pricing.ts ``` Then add `"angularCompilerOptions": { "basePath": "." }` to `projects/site/tsconfig.app.json` and build again. Both routes get `preload`, each page gets its own chunk's hint, and the stamps become `projects/site/src/app/…`. ### Exception or Error ```text None. The build succeeds and the pages render; only the lazy-route modulepreload hints are missing. ``` ### Your Environment ```text Angular CLI : 22.2.3 Angular : 22.2.3 Node.js : 24.20.0 Package Manager : npm 11.19.0 Operating System : darwin arm64 @angular/build 22.2.3 @angular/cli 22.2.3 @angular/common 22.2.3 @angular/compiler 22.2.3 @angular/compiler-cli 22.2.3 @angular/core 22.2.3 @angular/platform-browser 22.2.3 @angular/platform-server 22.2.3 @angular/router 22.2.3 @angular/ssr 22.2.3 typescript 6.0.3 ``` ### Anything else relevant? Also observed on 22.2.1, in our Nx workspace. The transformer's `relative(basePath, …)` is unchanged since it was introduced in 8d7a51dfc ("feat(@angular/ssr): add `modulepreload` for lazy-loaded routes").
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "@angular/build: lazy routes get no SSR modulepreload hints when the app's tsconfig is not at the workspace root (ɵentryName relative to basePath, chunk map relative to workspace root)" (#34369)

pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v12.11.2`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.11.2): pnpm 12.11.2 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.11.1...v12.11.2) This release fixes `--workspace-concurrency=Infinity`, filters set by an `updateConfig` hook, and store fetches with `enable-modules-dir=false`. ##### Patch Changes - `--workspace-concurrency=Infinity` now runs workspace projects with no concurrency limit. It used to fail with `invalid digit found in string` [#​16793](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16793). - `pnpm install` and other recursive commands now apply the `filter` and `filterProd` that an `updateConfig` hook sets. They used to run on every workspace project [#​16792](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16792). - `enable-modules-dir=false` now also fetches the packages an install reuses from an existing lockfile, so the store holds every package the lockfile lists. ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.11.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.11.1): pnpm 12.11.1 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.11.0...v12.11.1) This release fixes two ways `pnpm install` could fail, runs tools of any Rust release through `pnx`, and treats `registry.npmjs.com` as an alias of the npm registry. ##### Patch Changes - `pnpm install` no longer fails when `packageManager` pins the pnpm version that is already running and the registry does not publish that version. pnpm warns and continues. A registry mirror that has not synced a release no longer blocks the commands of a project pinned to it. - `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_CMD_SHIM_CHMOD` when `node_modules/.bin` holds a shim that another user created, if everyone can already execute it and it is not world-writable. This happens when several users share one checkout. - `enable-modules-dir=false` (`enableModulesDir: false` through the Node.js addon) fetches the registry packages the host can install into the store again, as pnpm v10 did, while still writing nothing under `node_modules`. The setting exists for a `node_modules` that something else mounts from the store, such as a FUSE daemon, and that consumer no longer has to download each package on first access. A plain `--lockfile-only` run still fetches nothing. - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` no longer put `.npmignore` and `.gitignore` files in the tarball. A `files` entry that names one still ships it. - pnpm now treats `https://registry.npmjs.com/` as an alias of `https://registry.npmjs.org/`. Registry requests, credentials, and trusted publishing use the canonical hostname. - `pnx --package=rust@ ` runs a tool of that Rust release, for example `pnx --package=rust@nightly-2026-01-01 cargo build`. pnpm installs the release with the components and targets from `rust-toolchain.toml` and the target of each `--target` argument. - `pnpm install` now links agent skills for more coding agents. It detects the agent from `ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT`, `COPILOT_AGENT`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `AI_AGENT`, and `CLAUDE_CODE` [pnpm/tasks#116](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/116). - When the registry rejects `pnpm stage publish`, the error message now starts with "Failed to stage package". ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.11.0): pnpm 12.11.0 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.10.1...v12.11.0) This release adds Rust toolchain management, links the agent skills that dependencies ship, adds the `permissions` setting, and keeps the colors of streamed script output. ##### Minor Changes - `pnpm install` now links the agent skills that direct dependencies ship under `skills//SKILL.md` into the project's agent skill directories, such as `.claude/skills`. A package's skills are linked only after you approve them with `pnpm approve`. The `skills.dirs` setting chooses the directories [pnpm/rfcs#35](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/rfcs/pull/35). Added the `permissions` setting, which records what each dependency may do. Its `build` capability works like `allowBuilds` and takes precedence over it. `pnpm approve-builds` writes to `permissions` when `pnpm-workspace.yaml` already has it, and to `allowBuilds` otherwise. Added `pnpm permissions`, which lists the granted and denied permissions and the packages awaiting approval. `pnpm approve` reviews build scripts and agent skills in one prompt [pnpm/rfcs#36](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/rfcs/pull/36). - pnpm now installs and runs Rust toolchains. - With `cargo.enabled`, `pnpm install` installs the toolchain named in `rust-toolchain.toml`. pnpm verifies the release signature, stores the toolchain once per machine, and links it into `.pnpm/rust`. `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` put its `cargo` and `rustc` on the `PATH`. - `pnpm add -g rust@` installs a toolchain globally. The `cargo` and `rustc` commands run it outside projects that pin their own. `pnpm update -g`, `pnpm ls -g`, and `pnpm remove -g` manage it like any global package. - In a project, `pnpm add rust@` pins the toolchain in `rust-toolchain.toml`. - `pnpm shim add rust` adds project-aware shims for `cargo`, `rustc`, and the other Rust tools. In a project with a `rust-toolchain.toml`, they run the toolchain the file names and install it on first use. Elsewhere, the next command of the same name on `PATH` runs, such as rustup's. - `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now keep the colors of script output that they print under the project's name, such as with `--stream`. pnpm sets `FORCE_COLOR=1` for these scripts when its own output is in color, unless `FORCE_COLOR` is already set. Script output is also rendered more cleanly: - A line that a progress bar redraws with `\r` shows only its last state. - Escape codes that move the cursor or clear the screen are dropped. - Long colored lines are cut at the terminal width. - `pnpm -r run` no longer garbles its live output when a script fails while other scripts are still running. ##### Patch Changes ##### Installing packages - pnpm no longer panics with "unexpected error when polling the I/O driver" when it runs under QEMU user-mode emulation, such as a `linux/amd64` container on an Apple Silicon Mac [#​16696](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16696). - `pnpm view`, `pnpm update`, and other commands that read registry metadata now work behind proxies that end a response by closing the connection without a TLS `close_notify` alert [#​16704](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16704). - pnpm now switches to the version a project pins in `packageManager` or `devEngines.packageManager` even when `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has a setting the running pnpm cannot read, such as a `lockfile.includeResolutionSettings` section. If pnpm does not switch, it still reports that setting [#​16675](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16675). - When the `pnpm` package has to download its native binary on first run, it now uses the registry and credentials from `.npmrc` and from the `npm_config_registry` and `pnpm_config_registry` environment variables. `COREPACK_NPM_REGISTRY` still takes precedence. A project `.npmrc` is not read when `COREPACK_INTEGRITY_KEYS` turns off the signature check [#​16655](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16655). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm add --config` now apply `minimumReleaseAge` when they resolve a config dependency. A config dependency range resolves to the newest version that is old enough, so a later clean `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` accepts the lockfile [#​16660](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16660). - `pnpm remove` with `catalogPrune` no longer removes catalog entries that `pnpm-lock.yaml` still records for workspace projects missing from disk. Before, a following frozen install failed with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` [#​16679](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16679). - With `cargo.enabled`, `pnpm install` now writes the source replacement for vendored crates into `.pnpm/crates/config.toml` and includes it as optional from `.cargo/config.toml`. A checkout without `.pnpm` builds with plain Cargo [#​16659](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16659). - With `nodeLinker.type` set to `loaded`, Node.js now stops with `ERR_PNPM_LOADER_UNSUPPORTED_NODE` when it preloads the store loader on a version the loader cannot serve. The supported versions are `^24.18.0 || >=26.2.0`. On other versions, CommonJS packages imported from ESM failed with `Cannot find module` on their first relative `require()`. - On Windows, `pnpm install` no longer fails with "The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect" when a package contains a file whose name is invalid on Windows, such as `icon.svg?as=metadata.d.ts`. pnpm removes the invalid characters from the name and prints a warning that lists the renamed files. - On Windows, hoisting no longer fails intermittently with link errors when a junction is created or replaced concurrently [pnpm/tasks#53](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/53). ##### Resolving dependencies - `pnpm install --no-optional` now installs the peer dependencies a project declares when `autoInstallPeers` is on. The lockfile marked such a peer `optional: true` when another dependency had it as an optional peer. - `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` now link an optional peer to the workspace package that the workspace root depends on when the picked version matches it. They installed the registry package with the same name and version [#​16706](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16706). - Removal overrides such as `"debug>supports-color": "-"` now also apply to an optional peer that a package declares only in `peerDependenciesMeta` [#​16681](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16681). - `pnpm add` and other installs that re-resolve dependencies now keep the locked `devEngines.runtime` version while it still satisfies the declared range [#​16764](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16764). - `pnpm audit --fix update` now updates only the dependencies whose locked version is vulnerable [#​14928](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14928). - `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update --interactive` now apply `overrides` before they look up the latest version. Before, a dependency overridden to an npm alias was compared with the latest version of the package the override replaces [#​16719](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16719). ##### Patched dependencies - Patches saved with CRLF line endings now apply, including a patch that creates or deletes a file. pnpm rejected the git headers of such a patch with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_PATCH` and the message `invalid file mode: 100644` [#​16641](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16641). - A patch that changes a file's mode, such as adding or removing the executable bit, now applies the new mode on Unix [pnpm/tasks#110](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/110). ##### Injected dependencies and deploy - With `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, an injected workspace package installed in the same run as its dependent now holds only the files its `files` field selects. The copy also held other files of the project, such as `tsconfig.json` [#​16683](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16683). - A script listed in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` no longer fails when it rewrites `package.json` while pnpm is copying its edits into the injected copies. The sync after the script now replaces a half-copied manifest. - `pnpm deploy` with a shared lockfile no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` for `settings.dedupeInjectedDeps` or `settings.dedupePeerDependents` when `lockfile.includeResolutionSettings` is enabled. The deployed lockfile now records both settings as `false`, the values the deploy installs with. - `pnpm deploy` now writes the dependencies in the deployed `package.json` sorted by name. It also sorts the `allowBuilds` entries in the deployed `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Repeated deploys of the same lockfile now produce identical files [#​16687](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16687). ##### Packing and publishing - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now match `.npmignore` and `.gitignore` rules the way npm does. A negation such as `!lib/**` or `!lib/**/!(*.map)` re-includes files under a directory that an earlier `*` rule excluded [#​16743](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16743). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` no longer always include root files that merely start with `README`, `LICENSE`, or `LICENCE`, such as `README_INTERNAL.md`. Only `README`, `LICENSE`, `LICENCE`, and `COPYING`, with or without an extension, ship regardless of `files` and `.npmignore`, as in npm [#​16753](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16753). - `pnpm publish --provenance=false` and `--no-provenance` now turn off provenance under trusted publishing, so a package can be published from a self-hosted runner. Setting `provenance: false` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` does the same [#​16721](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16721). ##### Speed and resource use - `pnpm install` hardlinks files from a group-writable or world-writable store again. pnpm copied every file from such a store into `node_modules` [#​16677](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16677). - A repeat `pnpm install` no longer imports patched packages and packages with build scripts again when nothing changed. Their builds no longer run again either. This happened when `recursiveInstall` was `false` or the project had a `file:` dependency [#​16705](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16705). - Verifying the lockfile against `trustPolicy` and `minimumReleaseAge` uses less memory. pnpm no longer keeps every published version's manifest of each checked package in memory until the install ends [#​16656](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16656). - `pnpm rebuild ` and `pnpm rebuild --pending` no longer read the manifest of every installed package to find build scripts. Only the selected packages are inspected and built. On a large `node_modules` served lazily, such as over a network or FUSE mount, this turned a rebuild of a few packages into a fetch of every package. - `pnpm rebuild` no longer removes and recreates `node_modules` when the settings recorded in `node_modules/.modules.yaml` differ from the current configuration. The rebuild runs the build scripts against the installed packages as they are. - `pnpm store prune` now compacts the store's `index.db` after removing package entries, so the file shrinks again [#​16717](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16717). ##### Registry commands - `pnpm whoami`, `pnpm bugs`, `pnpm docs`, `pnpm repo`, `pnpm star`, `pnpm unstar`, and `pnpm stars` now honor the `--registry` option. - `--registry` now takes precedence over a scope's configured registry for scoped packages in `pnpm access`, `pnpm view`, `pnpm repo`, `pnpm star`, `pnpm unstar`, `pnpm owner`, `pnpm deprecate`, `pnpm undeprecate`, `pnpm unpublish`, `pnpm dist-tag`, `pnpm team`, and `pnpm stage`. Without `--registry`, `pnpm access` now sends a scoped package or scope to the registry configured for that scope. - Registry commands now keep the path of a registry URL such as `https://example.com/npm/` when they build request URLs. This applies to `pnpm access`, `pnpm owner`, `pnpm ping`, `pnpm search`, `pnpm star`, `pnpm stars`, `pnpm team`, `pnpm unstar`, and `pnpm whoami`. - `pnpm view` now honors the network retry settings. - `pnpm repo` now fetches the repository URLs of several packages in parallel. ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors

Issues.Title: extractLicenses crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')" when using Module Federation shared modules with webpack >= 5.107
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

21.x (with webpack <= 5.106.2)

### Description

`@angular-devkit/build-angular:browser` production builds that use Module Federation `shared` modules (for example, via `@angular-architects/module-federation`) crash when `extractLicenses` is `true`.

The crash comes from `license-webpack-plugin` 4.0.2, a dependency of `@angular-devkit/build-angular`. webpack 5.107.0 (webpack/webpack#20860) changed `ProvideSharedModule.identifier()` from `provide module (scope) name@version = request` to `provide module (scope) name@version|request`. The plugin still parses the identifier with `filename.split('=')[1].trim()` (`dist/WebpackInnerModuleIterator.js`), which throws.

`@angular-devkit/build-angular` 22.2.x depends on webpack 5.111.0, so every Module Federation app on the webpack builder is affected unless it disables `extractLicenses` (and so loses `3rdpartylicenses.txt`).

`license-webpack-plugin` has had no commits since 2023. I reported the bug there as well: <LINK TO THE license-webpack-plugin ISSUE>.

Possible actions:
- patch, fork or vendor `license-webpack-plugin` in `@angular-devkit/build-angular`, or
- guard the `provide module` case (the fix is a few lines, see the linked issue).

### Minimal Reproduction

1. `ng new mf-app` (Angular 22), then `ng add @angular-architects/module-federation --type host`.
2. Make sure `webpack.config.js` declares at least one `shared` package (the default `shareAll(...)` is enough).
3. `ng build --configuration production` (with `extractLicenses: true`, the default for production).

### Exception or Error

```text
- Generating browser application bundles (phase: setup)...
✔ Browser application bundle generation complete.
An unhandled exception occurred: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI: 22.2.x
Node: 24.21.0
@angular-devkit/build-angular: 22.2.2
@angular-architects/module-federation: 22.0.0
webpack: 5.111.0
license-webpack-plugin: 4.0.2
OS: Linux
```

### Anything else relevant?

Workaround: apply the fix to `license-webpack-plugin` with `patch-package`. Setting `"extractLicenses": false` also avoids the crash, but then no license file is generated.

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): encapsulate library build state in BuilderState and ExecutionResult
Issues.Body:
Introduce `BuilderState` and `ExecutionResult` to replace `SingleBuildState`, `BuildActionResult`, `LibraryCompilationDiagnostics`, and manual `watchedCompilationFiles` parameter threading across the library builder pipeline.

`BuilderState` manages incremental compilation state, watched compilation files, pending compilation modifications across aborted watch iterations, and `ExecutionResult` diagnostic collection.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(@angular/build): encapsulate library build state in BuilderState and ExecutionResult" (#34355)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): export NormalizedAssetsPattern and avoid mutating input patterns
Issues.Body:
Export the `NormalizedAssetsPattern` interface from `normalize-asset-patterns.ts`, avoid mutating input `AssetPatternClass` objects in place, and simplify directory detection using `statSync(..., { throwIfNoEntry: false })`.

Also import `normalizeAssetPatterns` directly in `library/options.ts` and add test coverage for asset `ignore` patterns.

Issues.Title: module.register() in the prerender loader prints DEP0205 on Node 26
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

`@angular/build` registers its in-memory ESM loader with `module.register()`, which Node runtime-deprecated in Node 26. The call is in `src/utils/server-rendering/esm-in-memory-loader/register-hooks.js`:

```js
register('./loader-hooks.js', { parentURL: pathToFileURL(__filename), data: workerData });
```

`esm-in-memory-loader/utils.js` points `IMPORT_EXEC_ARGV` at that file, and `server-rendering/prerender.js` passes it as the `execArgv` of every prerender worker, so each worker prints DEP0205 to stderr during `ng build`.

Node runtime-deprecated the API in nodejs/node#62401, merged 2026-04-01 and labelled semver-major, so the warning starts at Node 26. `@angular/build` 22.2.2 declares `engines.node` as `^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`, so this is a supported Node version.

This is not an Angular regression, the code did not change, Node did.

### Minimal Reproduction

Any app with prerendering, built on Node 26:

1. `ng new repro --ssr` and keep prerendering enabled.
2. `ng build` on Node 26.
3. DEP0205 appears on stderr, once per prerender worker.

Measured on our app with Angular CLI 22.2.2, `@angular/build` 22.2.2, Node 26.5.0 on Windows, and on our CI agent (Linux, Node 26) in the production build step.

Also reproduced without a build, which isolates the loader from the rest of the pipeline. A worker created the way `prerender.js` creates one:

```js
const { Worker } = require('node:worker_threads');
const { IMPORT_EXEC_ARGV } = require('@angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/esm-in-memory-loader/utils.js');
new Worker('./stay-alive.cjs', {
  execArgv: [IMPORT_EXEC_ARGV],
  workerData: { outputFiles: {}, workspaceRoot: process.cwd() },
});
```

with `stay-alive.cjs` holding the worker open for a moment (`setTimeout(() => {}, 700)`). Without the flag it prints DEP0205 in 3 of 3 runs, with `NODE_OPTIONS=--disable-warning=DEP0205` it is clean in 3 of 3 runs.

Worth knowing when reproducing: DEP0205 is emitted asynchronously, so a worker whose body is `process.exit(0)` exits before the warning flushes and the run looks clean.

### Exception or Error

```text
(node:24372) [DEP0205] DeprecationWarning: `module.register()` is deprecated. Use `module.registerHooks()` instead.
(Use `node --trace-deprecation ...` to show where the warning was created)
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.2
Angular           : 22.2.1
Node.js           : 26.5.0
Package Manager   : pnpm 12.3.1
Operating System  : win32 x64

@angular-devkit/build-angular   22.2.2
@angular-devkit/core            22.2.2
@angular-devkit/schematics      22.2.2
@angular/build                  22.2.2
@angular/cli                    22.2.2
@angular/core                   22.2.1
@angular/platform-server        22.2.1
@angular/ssr                    22.2.2
rxjs                            7.8.2
typescript                      6.0.3
zone.js                         0.16.3
```

### Anything else relevant?

A possible fix, from reading the two hook files. `module.registerHooks()` takes synchronous hooks, and `loader-hooks.js` is almost there already: `initialize` and `resolve` are synchronous, and `load` has exactly one await, `await readFile(filePath)`, which `readFileSync` covers. The `data: workerData` channel is not needed either, because the hooks already run inside a worker that can read `workerData` directly.

The one real difference to weigh is that `registerHooks` runs the hooks on the calling thread rather than on a separate loader thread, so the synchronous read would block it.

The same Node 26 warning reported elsewhere, in case it helps: payloadcms/payload#18361 and Julien-R44/hot-hook#18.

What we do meanwhile: `NODE_OPTIONS=--disable-warning=DEP0205` on the build step, which silences only this code.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "module.register() in the prerender loader prints DEP0205 on Node 26" (#34358)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): use module.registerHooks() for in-memory ESM loader
Issues.Body:
Node.js 26 runtime-deprecates `module.register()` (`DEP0205`) in favor of synchronous `module.registerHooks()`.

Update the server-rendering in-memory ESM loader hooks to make `load` synchronous using `readFileSync` and register the hooks directly via `registerHooks({ resolve, load })`.

Closes #34358

Issues.Title: bug(material/menu): menu restores focus to its trigger after a menu item opens a dialog (animations disabled / prefers-reduced-motion)
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

 When a mat-menu item opens a MatDialog and animations are disabled (provideNoopAnimations / animations disabled, or the user's OS has reduced motion so `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches), the dialog ends up with no focus: focus is moved back to the menu trigger behind the dialog's backdrop.

Cause: with animations disabled the dialog's initial focus runs synchronously during the menu item's click (in the microtask after the click listener). The click then reaches the menu panel, which emits `closed('click')`, and `MatMenuTriggerBase._destroyMenu` calls `this.focus(this._openedBy)` unconditionally, without checking where focus currently is. With animations enabled the dialog focuses ~150ms later, after the menu has closed, so the problem doesn't show.

Since `prefers-reduced-motion` comes from an OS setting (e.g. Windows "Animation effects" off), regular users hit this, and keyboard and screen-reader users land on a control hidden behind the modal.

This was reported in #14879, which was closed as a duplicate of #11696 before the reporter clarified it only happens with NoopAnimationsModule; it was then locked. The menu code on `main` still restores focus unconditionally.

Possible fix, following the dialog's own guard from #17300 ("don't move focus if it was moved during close animation"): in `_destroyMenu`, when the close reason is `'click'`, skip restoring focus if it is already inside a different overlay pane (not the menu's own pane, not a menu panel such as a submenu, and not the overlay pane that contains the trigger itself). Every other close (Escape, Tab, backdrop click, programmatic close) keeps today's
behaviour. This doesn't change the accessibility position in #11696: focus still returns to the trigger whenever the menu owns it; it only stops the menu from pulling focus out of a modal that an item just opened. Happy to send a PR with tests if this direction is acceptable.

### Reproduction

  StackBlitz (from #14879, older Angular/Material):
  https://stackblitz.com/edit/checkbox-reactive-2zhjpp?file=app%2Fapp.component.ts

  I wasn't able to save a new StackBlitz, so this links the reproduction from #14879. The bug is not specific to that
  old version:

  - It reproduces on Angular 21.2.25 / @angular/cdk + @angular/material 21.1.2 in an application with animations
  disabled through the OS setting (Windows "Animation effects" off, so `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches and
  Material disables its animations). After a menu item opens a MatDialog, `document.activeElement` is the menu trigger
  behind the dialog's backdrop, not the dialog's `cdkFocusInitial` button.
  - The cause is unchanged on `main`: `MatMenuTriggerBase._destroyMenu` in `src/material/menu/menu-trigger-base.ts`
  still ends with

      if (this.restoreFocus && (reason === 'keydown' || !this._openedBy || !this._triggersSubmenu())) {
        this.focus(this._openedBy);
      }

    with no check of where focus currently is, so whenever the dialog takes focus before the menu finishes closing
  (always the case with animations disabled), the menu takes it back.

  Steps (old StackBlitz, which uses NoopAnimations):
  1. Open the StackBlitz and click the menu trigger.
  2. Click the menu item that opens the dialog.
  3. In the console, run `document.activeElement`: it is the menu trigger, not the dialog's button.

  Single-file reproduction for current versions (Angular/Material 21; paste as main.ts in a new Angular project):

  import {Component, inject} from '@angular/core';
  import {bootstrapApplication} from '@angular/platform-browser';
  import {MatButtonModule} from '@angular/material/button';
  import {MatMenuModule} from '@angular/material/menu';
  import {MatDialog, MatDialogModule} from '@angular/material/dialog';

  @Component({
    imports: [MatButtonModule, MatDialogModule],
    template: `
      <mat-dialog-content>Delete this item?</mat-dialog-content>
      <mat-dialog-actions>
        <button mat-button mat-dialog-close cdkFocusInitial>Cancel</button>
        <button mat-button [mat-dialog-close]="true">Delete</button>
      </mat-dialog-actions>
    `,
  })
  export class ConfirmDialog {}

  @Component({
    selector: 'app-root',
    imports: [MatButtonModule, MatMenuModule, MatDialogModule],
    template: `
      <button mat-button [matMenuTriggerFor]="menu">Menu</button>
      <mat-menu #menu="matMenu">
        <button mat-menu-item (click)="open()">Open dialog</button>
      </mat-menu>
    `,
  })
  export class App {
    private dialog = inject(MatDialog);
    open() { this.dialog.open(ConfirmDialog); }
  }

  bootstrapApplication(App);

  On 21, emulate reduced motion (DevTools > Rendering > "Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion: reduce", then
  reload) or set the OS animation setting off, then click Menu > Open dialog and check `document.activeElement`.

### Expected Behavior

Focus stays on the dialog's initial focus target (the "Cancel" button with cdkFocusInitial), showing its focus indicator, exactly as it does when animations are enabled. The menu should not move focus back to its trigger while an overlay opened by the menu item holds focus.

### Actual Behavior

The dialog opens, but focus is on the menu trigger ("Menu") behind the dialog's backdrop: document.activeElement is the trigger button with cdk-focused / cdk-mouse-focused. The dialog shows no focused control, Enter re-activates the hidden trigger, and Tab starts from outside the dialog. The dialog's FocusTrap did focus "Cancel" first; the menu's _destroyMenu then called focus() on the trigger. 

document.activeElement after the dialog opens: button.mat-mdc-menu-trigger  (the menu trigger, behind the backdrop)

### Environment

  - Angular: 21.2.25
  - CDK/Material: 21.1.2 (the same unconditional restore is still in src/material/menu/menu-trigger-base.ts on main)
  - Browser(s): Chrome <your version>; also reproduced in an embedded Chromium. Any browser with animations disabled or
  prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
  - Operating System: Windows 11 (Settings > Accessibility > Visual effects > Animation effects: Off)

Issues.Title: fix(multiple): allow aria tab and accordion panels without content directive
Issues.Body:
The `ngTabPanel` and `ngAccordionPanel` directives warn in dev mode that they need `ngTabContent` or `ngAccordionContent` to render, but content placed directly in a panel already renders. It's created eagerly and stays in the DOM, and the panel gets the `inert` attribute while hidden.

This removes the warning, making eager rendering a supported alternative to the content directive. A single tab group or accordion can then mix eager panels with lazy ones, which keep or remove their content depending on their own `preserveContent`.

Rendering eagerly also means the content is included in server-rendered HTML, unlike lazy content.

Fixes #33950

Issues.Title: fix(material/datepicker): update parse error with signal forms when value stays null
Issues.Body:
Fixes #33740.

When a datepicker input is bound to a signal form with `[formField]`, the `matDatepickerParse` error goes stale whenever the model value stays `null`:

- typing an unparseable value (e.g. `foo`) into an empty input does not add the error;
- erasing an unparseable value does not clear it, so the form stays invalid on an empty field (the case in the issue).

## Cause

Signal forms compute the errors of a CVA's legacy validators in a `computed` that re-runs when the control value changes or when the validator calls its `registerOnValidatorChange` callback. In `MatDatepickerInputBase._onInput()`, the `null` to `null` path calls `_cvaOnChange(null)`, which signal forms ignore because the value did not change, and it never calls `_validatorOnChange()`: that call was only in the branch for a non-null, unchanged date. Reactive forms don't hit this, because `setValue` always re-runs the validators.

## Fix

Call `_validatorOnChange()` whenever the parse state flips while the value stays the same, including `null` to `null`. The branch that already did this for an unchanged non-null date behaves as before.

With reactive forms, the `null` to `null` case with a changed parse state now also triggers `updateValueAndValidity()` after the `setValue(null)` call. It gives the same result, with one extra `valueChanges`/`statusChanges` emission in that case.

## Testing

Two tests in `datepicker.spec.ts` use a real signal form (`form()` + `FormField`). Both fail on `main` and pass with this change:

- typing `foo` into an empty input sets `matDatepickerParse`;
- setting a date, typing `foo`, then clearing the input removes it.

`//src/material/datepicker:unit_tests_chromium` (407 tests, including the date range input) and `//src/material/input:unit_tests_chromium` pass locally.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(material/datepicker): update parse error with signal forms when value stays null" (#33951)

Issues.Title: build: fix API docs extraction of directives and imported types
Issues.Body:
The ARIA and CDK API pages on angular.dev are missing information, because the API extraction can't resolve several imports:

- 8 aria directives are shown as classes, and their inputs and outputs as plain properties, because their host directives are imported from another package.
- The drag-drop target doesn't use the import map, so `@angular/core` doesn't resolve, and its imports of other cdk packages aren't available. Most of its directives and its NgModule are shown as classes, and their inputs and outputs as plain properties.
- Many types are shown as `any`.

The extraction doesn't report any of this, because it ignores Angular compilation errors.

## Changes

Extraction rule:
- Map an import map entry to its target's own entry point, and fail if it doesn't exist. Currently, the rule picks the shortest `index.d.ts` among the target and its dependencies, which maps `@angular/aria/private` to `src/cdk/platform/index.d.ts`.
- Resolve relative imports of files outside `srcs` to the type declarations among the inputs, by setting `rootDirs` to include the bin directory. This mirrors how `ts_project` sees sources and declarations. A new `deps` attribute provides declarations that the import map doesn't.
- Map wildcards of directory entries relative to the directory itself, so that subpath imports like `rxjs/operators` resolve.
- Treat missing compiled stylesheets as empty, since they aren't inputs of the action and don't affect the docs.
- Fail on Angular compilation errors.

Targets: all of them use the wrapper with the import map, and those with relative imports of other packages (aria, drag-drop and three cdk/testing targets) get `deps`.

## Effect on the generated docs

Compared with `main`, 46 of the 110 aria and cdk API pages change:
- 13 classes are shown as directives and one as an NgModule, and their inputs and outputs as such, e.g. `readonly id = input<string>()` instead of `readonly id: InputSignal<any>`, or `@Input('cdkDragData') data: T` instead of `data: T`.
- Types shown as `any` show their real type, e.g. `Signal<boolean>` instead of `Signal<any>`, or `Subject<{ source: DragRef<any>; event: MouseEvent | TouchEvent; }>` instead of `any` for `DragRef.started`.
- Members inherited from base classes that now resolve are listed.
- The `Combobox` page no longer links `DeferredContentAware` to `/api/aria/private/DeferredContentAware`, which doesn't exist.

No page or member is removed, and no type gets worse. The remaining `any`s are declared as such in the source.

## Testing

- Every docs target builds on `main` and on each commit. Comparing all fields of the generated JSON, each commit only changes what its message describes.
- Each fix is needed: removing it brings its errors or `any`s back. Moving the remaining cdk/testing targets to the wrapper and removing the unused import map entry don't change the output, and neither does the stricter entry point for the remaining import map entries, which already resolve to their own entry point.
- `bazel build //...`, `pnpm lint` and the aria/combobox unit tests pass.

Issues.Title: bug(aria/tabs): the tab list loses its only Tab stop when the active tab is removed after an interaction
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

When the tab that currently holds the roving `tabindex="0"` (the *active* tab, `TabListPattern.activeTab`) is removed from the tab list after the user has already interacted with the list, **no remaining tab gets `tabindex="0"`**. Every tab ends up with `tabindex="-1"`, so the tab list is no longer reachable with `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` (WCAG 2.1.1 / 2.4.3).

It is easy to hit with `selectionMode="explicit"`, where the active tab (focus) and the selected tab can differ, but the cause does not look specific to it: any removal of the active item after the first interaction should behave the same.

Cause, from reading the source (the guard is still on `main`): `TabListPattern.setDefaultState()` is the only place that re-assigns `activeItem`, and it is guarded.

```js
setDefaultStateEffect() {
  if (this.hasBeenInteracted()) return;   // never runs again after the first interaction
  this.setDefaultState();
}
// onKeydown / onClick / onFocusIn: this.hasBeenInteracted.set(true)
```

After the first focus / key / click, `hasBeenInteracted` stays `true`. If the active tab is then destroyed, `activeItem` still points to the removed tab, so no tab in `items()` matches and the roving `tabindex` is `-1` everywhere. Nothing falls back to the selected tab or to the first focusable tab.

A possible fix is to re-run the default-state logic when the active item is no longer part of `items()`, regardless of `hasBeenInteracted`:

```js
setDefaultStateEffect() {
  const active = this.activeTab();
  if (this.hasBeenInteracted() && active !== undefined && this.inputs.items().includes(active)) return;
  this.setDefaultState();
}
```

Related: #33934 (same area of code, but about a focus moved by a script, not about a removed active tab); #32969 / 0f5b0eee introduced the `hasBeenInteracted` guard.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/duypg9mo?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. `Tab` into the tab list (focus lands on `A`), press `ArrowDown` once: focus moves to `B`, which is now the active tab (`tabindex="0"`); `A` stays selected because the selection is explicit.
2. Press `Tab` three times: the panel itself, the input, then the `remove B` button.
3. Press `Enter` on `remove B`: the active tab `B` is destroyed.
4. Inspect the tabs: `A` and `C` both have `tabindex="-1"`.
5. Press `Shift+Tab` repeatedly: focus goes back through the input and the panel, then to the previous focusable element of the page. The tab list is skipped entirely.

Reproduced on `@angular/aria` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3.

### Expected Behavior

After the active tab is removed, a remaining tab (the selected one, else the first focusable) becomes the active tab and gets `tabindex="0"`, so the tab list keeps exactly one Tab stop.

### Actual Behavior

All tabs have `tabindex="-1"`. The tab list cannot be reached with `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`, and the arrow keys cannot help since focus cannot enter the list.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.1
- CDK/Material: `@angular/aria` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3, `@angular/cdk` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3
- Browser(s): Microsoft Edge (Chromium), also driven with real key events over the Chrome DevTools Protocol
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Windows 11

Issues.Title: bug(mat-datepicker): date parse errors are not propagated to Signal Forms
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

The datepicker input provides a matDatepickerParse validation error when the user enters text that cannot be parsed as a date.

This error is available when using Reactive Forms, but when using Signal Forms, the error does not reach the errors signal of the field tree. The value of the form field stays as `null`.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-d3y2q7gw?file=src%2Fmain.ts,src%2Fmain.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. Start the application.
2. Enter an invalid date string into the Reactive Forms datepicker.
3. Observe that the control reports a matDatepickerParse error.
4. Enter the same invalid date string into the Signal Forms datepicker.
5. Observe that the Signal Forms field does not report the corresponding parse error in field().errors().

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the date parse errors to also be available to the Signal Form.

If I understand correctly, this seems to be in line with the direction of the Angular Signal Forms API, for example with https://angular.dev/api/forms/signals/transformedValue to report parse errors in custom controls.

### Actual Behavior

The date parse errors are not available to the Signal Form. Since the form value remains as `null` for invalid values, distinguishing between an empty form and invalid input is not possible in the schema.

Issues.Title: bug(COMPONENT): Angular ARIA tab must allow eager loading of tab content
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

## Description

Angular Aria's tabs implementation appears to require tab panel content to be declared using `ng-template[ngTabContent]`, which prevents consumers from eagerly rendering tab panel content in the DOM.

This is problematic for use cases where all tab panels need to be initialized upfront, rather than lazily instantiated when their associated tabs become active. For example, a tab panel may contain a component that needs to initialize early, or preload data that is required for SEO (in SSR setup).

Currently, `ngTabContent` can only be applied to an `ng-template`, and the implementation warns when a tab panel does not contain the expected content directive. Applying `ngTabContent` directly to a component or a regular element does not work because it does not match the directive's selector.

It would be useful to provide a supported way to eagerly instantiate tab panel content while retaining the existing tab panel API and accessibility behavior.

## Reasoning

The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide recommends automatic tab activation on focus when the associated panel can be displayed without noticeable latency. It also notes that this typically requires panel content to be preloaded; otherwise, automatic activation introduces delays that significantly hinder efficient keyboard navigation.

Eager loading is therefore a legitimate use case for accessible tabs, particularly when panel content requires initialization or data fetching before it can be displayed.

Providing an explicit mechanism for eager content instantiation would allow developers to avoid unnecessary delays during tab navigation without having to implement their own tab behavior or work around the current content directive requirements.

### Reproduction

Link: https://angular.dev/guide/aria/tabs#example-1



### Expected Behavior

I expect the ngTabContent to have a selector on its own without the ng-template infront, so that the tab content can be eagerly loaded

### Actual Behavior

The ngTabContent selector has ng-template in front of it which prevents us from eagerly loading tab content that may contain useful information and is needed upfront and without layout shift

### Environment

- Angular: latest
- CDK/Material: N/A
- Browser(s): latest
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): N/A
